disposition: Dark chocolate review with separate background Parkinson and fortification mentions. No primary peanut-oil neurological endpoint.

Peanut oil disperses intramuscular curcumin prodrug suspensions. Reserpine hypothermia was the relevant behavioral readout. The drug formulation contrast does not isolate oil or measure a frozen endpoint.
Injected peanut oil did not change hippocampal neuron loss against the iron group. The original assessment already identifies the injected vehicle and histological endpoint.
Peanut oil extraction of radiolabelled reserpine from rat brain subcellular material. No dietary contrast or clinical outcome. Public accession has no abstract.
Peanut allergy series with two labial oil positives of 50 tested and pooled hoarseness. No verified oil-specific voice result or grade. Toulouse overlap unresolved.
Three positive labial oil challenges. Hoarseness is pooled across all tested foods. Oil grade, speech, and Parkinson outcomes unavailable.
Injected sterile oil control for hormonal effects on electrically stimulated rat tongue endurance. No dietary oil or clinical fatigue contrast.
Subcutaneous benzyl-benzoate/peanut oil depot compared two pyrimethamine preparations. Measured drug disposition and mortality.

Publisher-deposited complete abstract confirms stable or slightly increased posttetanic potentiation after oral oil vehicle and gradual variable decreases after toxicant exposure. Oil grade and an oil-free contrast were unavailable. Full paper remains pending.
Membrane rigidity concerns foodborne bacteria. There is no neurological symptom outcome.
CAPE versus DMSO/peanut oil vehicle in toxin-model Huntington disease. Rotarod evaluated the drug against a mixed carrier. Native text extractor rejected source license.
Groundnut oil was screened during patch development. Optimized in-vivo risperidone motor formulation used olive and jojoba oils.
Groundnut oil enhanced olanzapine penetration in vitro. Final optimized in-vivo rotarod and grip formulation used corn oil.
Peanut oil was held in an atherogenic rabbit diet. Rigidity refers to the artery wall, and calcium is the compared exposure.
Tamoxifen suspended in injected peanut oil in a Niemann–Pick C mouse model. Report discusses rotarod and drug effects without separate oral oil comparison.
Peanut-only versus peanut/rapeseed diet with low- and high-rotarod results. Only the low-apparatus effect was significant. No grade, handwriting or Parkinson outcomes.
Intrarectal peanut oil vehicle compared with an irritant in a genetically modified mouse model. Freezing and grimace measured without a standalone oral oil comparison.
Oil-type variable in lornoxicam depot development. The in-vivo arm measures pharmacokinetics, without a pain severity outcome.
Oral market and laboratory-stripped groundnut oil groups in adjuvant arthritis. Paw and inflammatory outcomes, without an analgesia endpoint.
Peanut oil in topical fluorouracil cream. Trial compared actinic keratosis clearance and local tolerability across different drug formulations.
Pain duration after injection of phenol, menthol and peanut oil for anal fissures. Uncontrolled retrospective series, with no standalone oil contrast.
Oral hormone formulations with or without peanut-oil-containing reference capsules. Main findings concern bioavailability and general safety.
Topically applied peanut oil and other solvents in blinded acute tape removal pain experiment. Group comparison p=.39, without a dietary contrast.
Topical steroid in a refined peanut/mineral oil blend. Assessed dermatitis, adrenal suppression and general adverse events in infants.
Formalin nociception after developmental bisphenol A exposure. The oil-only maternal group was vehicle comparison for controls, without an oil-free maternal group in the design.
Injected oleyl alcohol in sterile peanut oil to induce canine joint inflammation. Measured opioid receptor binding, without a behavioral pain outcome.
Oral peanut-oil vehicle in cannabinoid assay. Hot-plate response with drug and no oral writhing response. Later human trial used lactose rather than the animal vehicle.
Injection-site pain after vaccine with peanut-oil adjuvant versus aqueous formulation, 64% versus 35%. Exposure is a compound injectable and outcome is local pain incidence.
Predicted allergy risk from traces in highly refined vegetable oil. Modelling, without measured Parkinson symptoms.
Nasal product refined-oil identification in a practitioner awareness survey. No participant symptom measure.
Review of allergy to peanut oil formulations and reported reactions. Does not report a new clinical contrast on a frozen endpoint.
Controlled crude/refined oral allergy challenge already annotated and assessed. No acoustic voice measure or confirmation that crude oil is cold-pressed.
